learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the cutting edge of their field of study.
Basic knowledge on the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Topic 2. Basic data types and control structures
Script 4: Sequential structures, conditional structures, cyclic structures
assessment_rules: The final grade is the weighted sum of the qualifications obtained in theoretical concepts (70%) and laboratory practices (30%). Theoretical concepts are evaluated by a problem exam. Laboratory practices are evaluated during sessions with two exercises: programming (25% of the final grade) and databases (5% of the final grade). Students must obtain a minimum grade of 5 to pass the course. In extraordinary calls, the final grade will be obtained from a single exam covering both theoretical concepts and laboratory practices.
